messages.subject: quadratic relationship in mediation analysis
parts:
Hey everyone,

I would like to conduct a mediation analysis in lavaan. I would like to test the effect of age (in years) on a cognitive function, statistical learning (SL). I would like to test if 1) age predicts performance in SL, and 2) if so, this relationship is mediated by age effects in other cognitive factors (perceptual speed [PS], and working memory [WM]).

My mediation model would look like:
-- predictor variable: age
-- outcome variable: SL
-- mediator variables: PS and WM (I would like to include them both in a single model because if mediation occurs, I am curious if they mediate the same shared variability between age and SL)

However, my problem is that age effects in the case of all cognitive abilities (SL, PS and WM) are nonlinear (I think that a quadratic logarithmic function describes them best):


The relationship between the cognitive abilities are linear:



So the relationships (and regressions) within my model would look like:
-- c path: SL ~ age + age^2 (quadratic)
-- a paths: WM ~ age + age^2 and PS ~ age + age^2 (quadratic)
-- b paths: SL ~ PS and SL ~ WM (linear)

Common sense suggests me that this is something that I can test in a mediation analysis, and I also found some resources leading through a SEM assuming a quadratic relationship between a predictor and an outcome variable: https://youtu.be/KPvrbC3DXSY?si=90jfAqwt13Oh-GGk

I put this model together (age_years_log = log(age_years); age_years_log2 = log(age_years)^2):



And here is the output I got:



If I could put a good model together and I interpret my results correctly, based on significance values, this would mean that age has both a direct and an indirect effect through WM on SL.

However, even if all this is correct, I have a hard time interpreting the effect sizes. First, the coefficients mean two different dimensions (linear trend and curvature, if I understand well), so it doesn't seem to be reasonable to combine them into a single number. But more importantly, second, the standardized coefficients are ridiculously large. I suspect this has something to do with the nonstandardized age variable (or with the entire model being wrong)!

My main questions are:

1) Is this whole analysis with quadratic relationships between some of the variables a viable mediation analysis in lavaan? If not, what kind of analysis would you suggest instead?

2) If this mediation analysis can be done, how could I get effect sizes for the different paths?

Any insight is greatly appreciated! :)

Cheers,
Kriszti
